Theorem
[Dirichlet problem]

Source: petersen:page-0422 ↗ thm:pet-ch11-schauder-estimates 1. ch11:11.2.4On a bounded smooth domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb {R}^n$, the problem $Lu=f$, $u|_{\partial \Omega }=\varphi $ has a unique solution $u\in C^{2,\alpha }(\Omega )$ when $f\in C^\alpha (\Omega )$, $\varphi \in C^{2,\alpha }(\partial \Omega )$.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch11-dirichlet-problem-unique-solution \sketch The Schauder theory supplies a solution. If $u_1,u_2$ solve the same data, $w=u_1-u_2$ satisfies $Lw=0$ and vanishes on $\partial \Omega $; the maximum principle gives $w=0$.

□
